newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ansett Australia says profits thin on the ground.
newsitem.headline: Ansett Australia says profits thin on the ground.

text.p: Loss-making airline, Ansett Australia, on Wednesday foreshadowed another poor result for the current year to June 30, saying profits were thin on the ground.

Asked if Ansett would be profitable this year, managing director Rod Eddington said: "The implications for profits are in a sense self-evident. Part of that is a function that we are trying to build an international network from scratch."
"Profits ... are thin on the ground," he told aviation reporters in Melbourne.

Ansett, half owned each by News Corp Ltd and Air New Zealand, has recently begun a two to three year programme of turning around the core airline business, and so far was broadly on target for its goals to improve revenue and cut costs.
"Those targets were broadly being met. We are not quite there on the cost savings front," he said.
